pack.title: Retail pressure
pack.description: Make a purchase decision at your own pace.

scenarios.setting: You are considering a jacket and the salesperson insists you buy immediately.
scenarios.jab: Someone else will buy it if you walk away.
scenarios.goal: Make a purchase decision at your own pace.

replies.line: I can accept that. I'm taking time to decide.
replies.why: Accepting the possibility of missing out removes the pressure to act immediately.
replies.delivery: Keep “taking time” firm; do not start listing reasons you need permission to leave.

replies.why: It declines the urgency without debating whether the scarcity is real.
replies.delivery: Say “I'll take that chance” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Do not start listing reasons you need permission to leave.

replies.line: Thanks for letting me know; I'll decide after I've had time to think.
replies.why: It receives the information while retaining control of the decision.
replies.delivery: Keep “Thanks for letting me know” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Do not start listing reasons you need permission to leave.

replies.line: My wallet doesn't do speed dating.
replies.why: The joke targets your buying pace rather than the salesperson.
replies.delivery: Keep “My wallet doesn't do speed dating” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Do not start listing reasons you need permission to leave.

followUp.jab: I can hold it only until closing.
followUp.line: Thanks; if it's gone when I return, I'll choose something else.
followUp.why: It acknowledges a real deadline without letting it determine your purchase.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “Thanks,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
